en: Theragāthā 6.7 Chakkanipāta,
First Chapter (Paṭhamavagga)
The Verses of the Elder Kātiyāna:
“Arise, Kātiyāna, sit up!
Do not be full of sleep; be watchful.”
Let not the King of Death, like a crooked fisherman, conquer you— the indolent one, the kinsman of negligence—
just as the surge of the great ocean [overcomes all].
Thus does birth and old age revolve; therefore,
make yourself your own island,
for no other refuge exists for you.
For the Teacher has conquered this path,
having transcended the bonds of birth, old age, and fear; being diligent throughout the first and last watches of the night, he has reached the goal.
Devote yourself to this; apply yourself with firm diligence.
Cast off those former bonds—you who wear the outer robe, whose feet are calloused, and who subsist on alms.
Do not indulge in the delight of play, nor in sleep;
meditate, Kātiyāna. Meditate, Kātiyāna, and conquer!
You are skilled in the paths to security from bondage;
having attained supreme purity,
you will go out like a flame by means of water.
Like a slender creeper that produces light,
you are bent by the wind;
even so, you remain unattached.
Shake off Māra, O you of the same clan as Indra!
Being free from passion for feelings,
wait for your time right here, having become cooled.
...the Elder Kātiyāna...
